summary: Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University, where they studied under Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2009).

Jinshi Fan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University (~1958–1963), she served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1998–2014) and held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He held positions at Tokyo National Museum (~1956–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1988–1994), Bukkyo University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) was an Indian history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendranath Mohanty (1928–2023) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1947–1949) and the University of Göttingen (~1952–1954). He taught at the University of Calcutta (~1955–1970), University of Oklahoma (~1972–1986), and Temple University (~1986–2008).
Jitsuaki Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and served as a professor at Toyo University (~1968–1989).

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1938–1942), he served as director of the Institute of World Religions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2000).

Joachim Gentz works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He has served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna in 1994, where he studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Leiden University (~1923–1924), he held posts at Leipzig University (~1924–1935) and as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1945–1955).
Joan Halifax (b. 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College (~1960–1964) and the University of Miami (~1968–1973).

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969), she spent her career at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–2022), serving as professor.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Chicago (~1971–1976). She held appointments at the University of Massachusetts Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (~1999, 2002).

Joe Bransford Wilson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (PhD 1984), taught at the University of Virginia (1981–1985), and served at UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (b. 1947) specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of London (~1966–1970), he served at the British Museum (1970–2010), including as Keeper of Coins and Medals.
Joey Hung (b. 1991) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts and held a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College (~2008).
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Bangabasi College and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held teaching posts at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog (b. 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing his PhD at Indiana University (~1995–2000), he became a professor at Southern Methodist University (~2001).
Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a linguist who held positions at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1826–1852) and the Bavarian State Library (~1829–1852).
